We want to hand this over to implementation next week and align on the quality monitoring (prompt sets, eval harness integration, regression alerts, and canary/rollback policy).

High-level ask: can your team confirm access to a staging endpoint and share a 100–200 sample of typical user prompts by EOD Friday (Jul 17)? That will let us wire the eval harness and run the initial regression baseline.

Proposed sequence (short):
- Day 0–2: access and credential exchange; confirm sample corpus
- Day 3–5: eval harness integration in staging; ingest prompt_harbor_v1.csv and run baseline
- Day 6–7: short canary (48-hour ramp for 5% traffic) with regression alerts active

Key SLAs we want to track during canary: latency P95, quality score (as defined in the eval spec), and hallucination rate. We usually recommend an automated regression alert threshold of a 5% drop in overall quality score OR a 3% absolute increase in hallucinations. Aditya and Marissa will include concrete rules.

CCing Marissa and Sean from implementation. Marissa — can you add the integration checklist and any gaps we should flag before the kickoff?

Thanks,

Samantha — quick answers inline and details below.

On Wed, Jul 15, 2026 at 08:04 AM Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm whether the eval harness requires an agent running inside our VPC or if we can point to Redwood's hosted harness for the baseline run?

We support both approaches: for regulated datasets we recommend running a lightweight eval agent inside your VPC (containerized; minimal outbound to our metrics ingestion endpoint). For an initial baseline run on synthetic/public prompt sets you can also point to our hosted harness. We'll leave the choice to ACME. If you want VPC execution we'll need an image pull and IAM role details.

> 2) For the regression alerts you mentioned, will those fire to our PagerDuty or to a Redwood monitoring channel first?

We can do either. Our standard is to send alerts into the customer's PagerDuty integration (we only page on signal-critical events). We'll also create a Redwood internal incident thread and notify the CS/Implementation owners.

Marissa — here's a starter integration checklist for implementation (attached as eval_harness_integration_spec.md). Highlights:
- Confirm staging endpoint & test API key (ACME gives)
- Upload prompt_harbor_v1.csv to the harness; map columns (prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_behavior_tag)
- Run baseline job (N=200) to compute quality_score & hallucination_rate
- Configure canary policy: 48h ramp, traffic steps at 5%, 25%, 60%, with auto-halt on regression condition
- Configure rollback tags (model_version -> tag so we can revert to previous model if needed)

I'll schedule the Monday Jul 20 10:00am PT kickoff. Sean — can you confirm the canary traffic ramp syntax and whether 48h total window is fine for your SRE constraints?

Laura

Attachments: eval_harness_integration_spec.md (Markdown stub)

Thanks — adding a few implementation notes from the integration side: 

1) Prompt mapping: please ensure your sample CSV uses the header fields exactly as in the spec (prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_behavior_tag). If you prefer to use an existing internal ID, we'll map it but need a stable key.

2) Eval harness config: the harness accepts a small config YAML (see snippet in eval_harness_integration_spec.md). Important flags: sampling_seed (for deterministic sampling), scoring_metrics (we default to a blended quality score; you can add custom scorers), and test_corpus_path (S3/GCS or local path for VPC agent).

3) Canary and rollback: we recommend tagging pre-canary model as v1.0-precandidate and during rollout creating a canary tag v1.0-canary-01. If regression alerts trigger, the automatic rollback uses the v1.0-precandidate tag. We also ask ACME to keep a labeled golden-set of ~300 prompts that are not exposed to live traffic for offline regression checks.

4) Access: we'll need a staging API key with the scope: read:prompts, write:eval-jobs, run:canary. If you'll run the harness inside your VPC, we need a short-lived service principal or an OIDC role mapping.

Example command to run baseline harness (hosted harness):

  ./redwood-eval run --input prompt_harbor_v1.csv --cfg eval_config.yaml --output baseline_20260717.json

Marissa
Implementation Engineer
Redwood Inference

Following up with concrete guardrail numbers and an alerting recommendation:

- Primary quality metric: blended_quality_score (combines correctness, instruction-following, and safety signals). Baseline will produce a moving average.
- Regression alert criteria (suggested): trigger if blended_quality_score drops by >= 5% relative to baseline (30-day rolling) OR hallucination_rate increases by >= 3 percentage points vs baseline.
- Secondary alerts: latency P95 > 2x baseline or error rate > 0.5% for 15m window.

Automation notes:
- We'll create an eval job that runs every 6 hours during canary and computes the metrics against the golden-set and live-sampled prompts.
- Canary ramp plan: 5% -> 25% -> 60% over 48 hours, with auto-halt if any primary regression condition fires (investigate window 10–30 minutes).

Rollback mechanics: when an auto-halt occurs we immediately tag traffic to the previous stable tag and trigger a post-mortem run of the eval harness with the golden-set. For auditability we push the failing job and evaluation artifacts to the ACME shared Drive folder.

I'll add the alert rules to the shared Drive folder under /monitoring/rules/ACME.

Aditya
